newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdogs see sense in power and gas marriage.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdogs see sense in power and gas marriage.

text.p: Regulation of British gas and electricity industries could be merged at some stage in the future, once opening up of these markets to full competition was completed, regulators said on Thursday.
Gas industry regulator Clare Spottiswood said it made sense to combine regulation as the two markets were moving closer togther.
"I think the two markets are coming together so I don't see why there shouldn't be one regulator in time," she said in response to questions.

Her counterpart in electricity Professor Stephen Littlechild said it might be sensible to merge the two funtions at some stage. But he said each had its work cut out currently to cope with the transition to a completely free market. "In due course it would be worth looking at," Littlechild said.

On the timing of the introduction of full competition in electricity, due by April next year, Littlechild said it was a tight schedule and electricity companies were saying how difficult it was going to be.
Littlechild, who was speaking at an industry conference, said currently Offer was looking at starting with 10 percent of customers from April 1 and phasing the rest in over six months.
He said they were working on where the initial 10 percent would be.

Spottiswood said the opening up of the domestic gas market to full competition was supposed to take place on a single day, sometime next year. But she said a phased introduction in 1998 was more likely.
